page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). The instance relies on x86_64 architecture with support for AVX, BMI2, and hardware-accelerated encryption via AES and SHA-NI instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions. It includes no bundled local storage and features no discrete GPU accelerators. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded performance paired with constrained overall throughput. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0 and PassMark encryption score of 4270.77, both placing in the middle 50% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 23.96 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded metrics reveal bottlenecks under intense load: PassMark CPU scored 5590.46, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 18.36 GB/sec (bottom 10%), and Geekbench multi-core performance reached 2939.0. Memory bandwidth delivers 31.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 16.16 GB/sec for large writes, while static web serving throughput reached 4.07 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 compute-to-memory balance and absence of integrated local NVMe storage, the ecs.c6a.xlarge provides an entry-level compute tier for lightweight background tasks and moderate processing workloads. It is best aligned with batch data processing, software build workers, light web serving, and stateless compute nodes that utilize network-attached block volumes. Deployments requiring intense vector operations, high database concurrency, or sustained heavy I/O will face limitations due to the lack of AVX-512, sub-optimal multi-core scaling, and 2 Gbps baseline network capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. It provides 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM distribution, and operates over the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 platform. The instance contains no integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block volumes for persistence, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark results show average single-thread performance, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0 and 23.96 GB/sec in gzip compression, alongside lower multi-threaded outcomes such as a 2939.0 Geekbench multi-core score and 4.07 GB/sec static web throughput. The server fits lightweight computational tasks, CI/CD build agents, and stateless web application serving where massive memory capacity or extreme parallel throughput is not required.
